"..."
"And it's weird how much I like you."
en.editorNote: A three-step play on the word 'weird' — the opener feels like the start of a complaint, the second beat partially defuses it, and the third sneaks in the confession. Delivered face-to-face, it creates that perfectly awkward-but-adorable pause.
variations: You're being weird today. How? Weirdly distracting — I can't focus because of you.
You've been strange lately. Where? Strangely showing up in all my dreams.

items.sourceNote: inspired by 2026 TikTok viral pickup lines list (duet/content theme), rewritten

zh-tw.editorNote: 用『合拍』雙關，第一秒以為要叫對方拍短影音，下一秒直接拉到一輩子的層次，落差感剛好，網路族群很吃這套
variations: 我們來個 duet 吧。剪輯什麼？剪輯我們以後的每一天
你願意跟我合拍嗎？拍什麼？拍一張全家福那種

"Like on TikTok?"
"No, like for the rest of our lives."
en.editorNote: Plays on the word 'duet' — sounds like a casual content-creation invite, then pivots into a lifelong commitment. The gap between casual and serious is what makes it land with chronically-online audiences.
variations: Let's collab. On a video? No, on a future.
Wanna be in my next post? Sure, what kind? The kind that lasts forever.

variations: 你猜我口袋裡有什麼？空的。為什麼？因為要留位置給你的手
你猜我兩隻手在幹嘛？沒幹嘛，剛剛好可以一隻牽你、一隻摸你頭

en.editorNote: A question-then-gesture combo. Best when you actually reach out right after the punchline lands — turns a corny line into a real moment. Perfect for the last mile of a will-they-won't-they situation.
variations: Guess what's in my pocket? Nothing. Why? I left room for your hand.
Guess what both my hands are doing? Nothing — one's free to hold yours, the other's free to mess with your hair.

items.sourceNote: inspired by 2026 AI/algorithm pickup line trend, rewritten

「因為你完全符合我心裡的那個 prompt。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 2026 年大家對 AI 都很熟，用 prompt 當比喻反而比星星月亮新鮮，講給工程師、設計師、行銷圈聽特別有效，搭配一秒停頓更殺

你是不是被 fine-tune 過？每個細節都剛好打中我

"Were you trained by an AI?"

"Because you match every single prompt I had in my head."
en.editorNote: In 2026 everyone gets AI references, so 'prompt' lands fresher than moon-and-stars. Especially deadly with engineers, designers, and anyone in marketing. Pause for a beat before the punchline.
variations: Are you my system prompt? Every time I think of you, my output gets weird.
Were you fine-tuned? Because every detail about you hits exactly right.

I did something wrong. What? I wrote you into the outline of my future.

Something's wrong with my coffee. What? I can't taste it when you're across the table.

Twenty-four hours in a day, know which ones I treasure most? The ones you're sleeping? No — the ones we're talking.

zh-tw.editorNote: 英文界經典『把U和I排在一起』的中文化版本，注音梗讓台灣人特別有共鳴，文具店、書局約會的時候用最自然，學生族群通殺
variations: 你會拼音嗎？會啊。那幫我把『你』跟『我』拼在一起，永遠不要拆開
倉頡輸入法你熟嗎？還行。那幫我打一個字，就是『你我』合體那種

en.content:
"You good with the alphabet?"

en.editorNote: Reworks the classic alphabet line into a dialogue setup. The casual 'why?' bait makes the cheesy payoff hit harder. Works in any text thread or casual chat.
variations: You know spelling? Yeah. Then spell 'us' for me — leave no space in between.
You good with letters? I am. Cool, because I want to put U right after I, no commas, no breaks.

items.sourceNote: map/getting-lost trope, freshly rewritten with conversational setup

zh-tw.content:

zh-tw.editorNote: 把舊版「你有地圖嗎」升級成Google Map更貼近生活，後半句「導航也救不了我」把無可救藥的喜歡感拉滿，路癡朋友拿來用特別有說服力
variations: 你有開定位嗎？沒有。難怪，我整顆心都找不到回去的路了

en.content:
"Hey, do you have Google Maps on you?"
"No, why?"
"Nothing — I'm already lost in your eyes and GPS can't save me anyway."
en.editorNote: Updates the dusty 'do you have a map' classic with a phone-era twist. The 'GPS can't save me' button adds self-aware cheesiness — works even better if you're known for being directionally challenged.
variations: Is your location on? It's not. Figures — my heart can't find its way back either.
You good with Uber? Yeah. Can you book one for me? From 'just friends' to your place.

items.sourceNote: coffee/latte pun trope, rewritten with bilingual wordplay

variations: 你愛喝拿鐵嗎？還好。那我請你，順便告訴你我超愛『拿』你的手
美式還是拿鐵？拿鐵。難怪我看你眼神這麼濃，化都化不開

en.content:
"Do you know how to order coffee?"
"Yeah, why?"
"Get me a latte — because I like you a latte."
en.editorNote: The 'a latte / a lot' pun is a coffee-shop classic for a reason. Works best when delivered with a straight face right before they catch the pun. Bonus points if you actually buy them the latte.
variations: What's your coffee order? An espresso. Cool — because you espresso everything I've been looking for.
You into mochas? A little. Because you mocha me happy every time I see you.

items.sourceNote: wifi/connection tech trope, rewritten with dialogue setup

en.content:
"Hey, what's your Wi-Fi password?"
"Why?"
"Oh nothing — I just feel like we already connected, but the signal's weak. Thought I'd get closer."
en.editorNote: Upgrades the basic 'are you Wi-Fi' line by making it a real-life situation. The 'getting closer for better signal' button gives you a smooth excuse to physically lean in.
variations: Is your Bluetooth on? No. That explains it — I've been trying to pair with you all night.
How many bars are you getting? Full bars. Cool, can I stand here? My signal's been dead since I saw you.

items.sourceNote: pineapple/fineapple food pun, rewritten with conversational hook

variations: 你喜歡吃芒果嗎？喜歡。那你就是我的芒果乾，越想越甜
你愛吃西瓜嗎？愛啊。那剛好，我想當你心裡那片最甜的

en.content:
"What's your favorite fruit?"
"Probably pineapple."
"Same — well, you actually. Because you're a total fineapple."
en.editorNote: Sets up the 'fineapple' pun with an innocent food question, so the cheesy reveal lands harder. Perfect for grocery store small talk or any meal-prep small talk on a date.
variations: You into mangoes? Yeah. Makes sense — you've got that 'man-go anywhere with you' energy.
Watermelon or strawberry? Watermelon. Cool, because one look at you and I'm already smitten.

items.sourceNote: time traveler/future trope, rewritten with dialogue framing

zh-tw.content:

zh-tw.editorNote: 把『時空旅人看見未來』的西方梗，換成台灣人熟悉的八字命理，文化在地化做得很到位，廟口、算命攤約會直接無敵，老一輩的也接得住
variations: 你信塔羅嗎？有點。那不用算了，我抽到的每一張都指向你
你看過你的命盤嗎？看過。我的不用看，反正主星是你

en.content:
"Do you believe in fortune telling?"
"Not really, why?"
"Doesn't matter — I already checked our future, and your name's the only thing on the page."
en.editorNote: Swaps the overused 'are you a time traveler' for a more grounded fortune-telling setup. Lets you sound confident and a little mysterious without sounding like a sci-fi nerd.
variations: You into astrology? A bit. Cool — my chart literally just says 'find them' with your photo attached.
Do you read tarot? Sometimes. No need to shuffle — every card I pulled tonight had your face on it.

items.sourceNote: coffee-themed pickup riff, rewritten as dialogue with everyday morning context

zh-tw.content:
「你今天喝咖啡了嗎？」

zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在早上見面、約咖啡、或加班場合丟出來，把日常的『缺咖啡』情境順勢轉成告白，土歸土但很貼生活，對方比較容易笑出來
variations: 你今天喝咖啡了嗎？沒。難怪我精神一直不好，看來我上癮的不是咖啡，是你
你早餐吃了沒？還沒。我也是，因為今天的『甜點』我想留給你

en.content:
"Have you had coffee yet today?"
"Not yet, why?"
"That explains it — I've been dragging all morning. Turns out I wasn't low on caffeine. I was low on you."
en.editorNote: Perfect for morning meetups, coffee dates, or office banter. The 'low on caffeine' setup feels grounded in daily life, so the cheesy pivot lands lighter and gets an actual laugh instead of an eye roll.
variations: Have you had coffee yet? Nope. Same — guess my real addiction isn't espresso, it's you.
Did you grab breakfast? Not yet. Me neither — I was saving room for something sweeter, like you.

items.sourceNote: fine-print / read-between-the-lines trope, rewritten as conversation

zh-tw.content:

variations: 你會看書本上的小字嗎？有時候會。那你要看仔細，因為我心裡最小的那行字寫著你
你讀書專心嗎？普通。那糟了，我怕你錯過我這頁最重要的一句話

en.content:
"Do you actually read the fine print?"
"Sometimes. Why?"
"That's good — because the most important line of my whole life has your name on it."
en.editorNote: Reworks the classic 'you'd be the fine print' line into a dialogue that earns its punch. Works well in bookstores, libraries, or quiet coffee shops where a soft, bookish tone fits the room.
variations: Do you read every page? Mostly. Good — because the most important sentence in mine has your name in it.
Are you a careful reader? I try to be. Then don't skip my next line — it's about you.

items.sourceNote: dessert / saved room trope, rewritten as natural dinner dialogue

zh-tw.content:
「你吃飽了嗎？」

zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在吃飯、約會、宵夜場合用，把『胃裡留位置給甜點』的日常梗自然延伸成告白，順口又不會太尬，餐桌上很容易接話
variations: 你吃飽了嗎？飽了。那糟糕，我胃裡那塊『甜點專屬位』突然只想裝下你
晚餐還吃得下嗎？快不行了。可惜，我本來想推薦今晚最甜的——就是你

en.content:
"Are you full yet?"
"Pretty much, why?"
"Damn — I was saving room for dessert, but now that spot only wants to be reserved for you."
en.editorNote: Best used at dinner, late-night snacks, or after a shared meal. The 'saving room for dessert' setup is so universal it doesn't feel forced, and the pivot to flirting reads as playful rather than corny.
variations: Got any room left? Barely. Shame — that dessert slot in my stomach is suddenly only craving you.
Still hungry? Not really. Too bad — I was about to recommend the sweetest thing on the menu, which is you.

items.sourceNote: Google / search-themed pickup, rewritten with everyday phone setup

variations: 你常Google東西嗎？常啊。那不用找了，你最想搜的那個答案就在眼前
你會用ChatGPT嗎？會。那省點token，你想問的那個人，已經在跟你說話了

"Do you Google stuff a lot?"
"Yeah, pretty often. Why?"

en.editorNote: Modernizes the classic 'are you Google' line by letting the other person say yes first, so the punchline lands as a reveal instead of a setup. Works great in cafes, study sessions, or any phone-out moment.
variations: Big Googler? Definitely. Then close the tab — what you're looking for is already right here.
You use ChatGPT a lot? Sometimes. Save the prompt — the answer you want is already talking to you.

items.sourceNote: photographer / picture-us-together line, rewritten as casual dialogue

zh-tw.editorNote: 土味中帶點浪漫，適合在旅遊、看展、拍照打卡的場合用，先丟一個無壓力的問題，再順勢把『腦中合照』講出來，比一上來就告白舒服很多
variations: 你會拍照嗎？普通而已。沒差，反正我心裡早就有一張我們合照

"That's okay — I've already taken a picture of us together in my head."

variations: Any good with a camera? Not really. No worries — I already snapped a picture of us in my mind.
Do you edit photos? Nope. Perfect — our picture doesn't need editing, you look great in every frame.

Latte or black? Latte. Knew it — sweet, smooth, and somehow I can't put you down.

items.sourceNote: rainy-day shelter pickup, rewritten as natural dialogue

「外面雨好像越下越大欸。」

en.content:
"The rain's really picking up out there."
"Yeah, kind of annoying actually."
"Wanna duck somewhere? I've had a spot reserved for a while now."
en.editorNote: Free opener whenever the weather cooperates. The trick is delivering 'a spot reserved' casually, like you're talking about a seat at a cafe — overplay it and it tips into corny. Works at bus stops, awnings, convenience stores.
variations: Rain's getting worse. Definitely. Wanna wait it out? There's a seat with your name on it.
This downpour's brutal. For real. Come hide out — I happen to have room, no cover charge.

items.sourceNote: Wi-Fi connection pickup, rewritten with phone-borrowing scenario

en.editorNote: Refresh of the classic Wi-Fi line — leading with a real-sounding signal question makes the punchline feel like a sudden realization instead of a setup. Smile through the last line; deadpan tips it into creepy territory.
variations: Got good signal? Pretty much. Makes sense — mine spikes to full whenever you're around.
Can you check your bars? All full. Figured — our connection's been stable since the second you sat down.

items.sourceNote: calendar / save-the-date pickup, rewritten with weekend planning dialogue

zh-tw.content:
「你這週末有空嗎？」

假日有計畫嗎？沒有。那好辦了，我的計畫永遠只有一個，就是你

en.content:

"Probably, why?"
"Nothing — just want to block it off, because honestly the only recurring event on my calendar is you."
en.editorNote: Doubles as actually asking them out, which is half the appeal. Throw away the 'recurring event' line quickly instead of landing it like a punchline — the casualness is what sells it. Best with someone you've already been chatting with.
variations: Saturday open? I think so. Cool, blocking it off — top of my calendar's always you anyway.
Got weekend plans? Not really. Easy — my plan's been the same for a while now, and it's you.

items.sourceNote: magician 'everyone disappears' classic, rewritten as crowded-bar dialogue

zh-tw.editorNote: 魔術師款『其他人都消失了』的對話版，從抱怨人多切入超自然。夜店、市集、跨年場、演唱會都好用。最後一句要看著對方眼睛講，但語氣要輕，不然會變偶像劇

en.content:
"This place is so packed tonight."

en.editorNote: Dialogue version of the classic magician 'everyone else disappears' line. Starting with a shared complaint about the crowd makes the reveal feel organic. Made for clubs, markets, concerts, NYE — anywhere busy. Soft delivery, eye contact, no theatrics.
variations: Crazy crowd tonight. Insane. Hadn't noticed — been kind of locked in on you the whole time.
It's wall-to-wall in here. So packed. Weird, I haven't seen anyone but you all night.

variations: What's your usual coffee order? Just noting it down for when I ask you out.
I blamed the coffee for keeping me up, then realized I was just thinking about you.

variations: I don't need the café Wi-Fi — the signal between us is already full bars.
You must be my hotspot, because I auto-connect the second I see you.

items.sourceNote: space 'rearrange the solar system to put U and I together' line, reimagined with original phrasing

「什麼事？」
「把『你』跟『我』這兩顆星，放到隔壁。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合看星星、頂樓夜景、或聊到天文話題時順勢丟出。走浪漫路線而非搞笑，講完可以接著指天上某顆星說『那顆就當作我們的』。室內也能用，把星空換成手機桌布
variations: 全宇宙的星星我都不想動，只想把你那顆移到我旁邊
別人看星座，我只想找一個位置，剛好讓你我並排

en.content:
"If I could rearrange the whole night sky, I'd only do one thing."
"What's that?"
"Move the star called 'you' right next to the one called 'me.'"
en.editorNote: Best for stargazing, rooftop views, or any moment astronomy comes up. Lean romantic rather than goofy; follow it by pointing at a star and saying 'that one's ours.' Works indoors too — swap the sky for a phone wallpaper.
variations: I wouldn't touch a single star in the universe — except to slide yours next to mine.
Everyone reads their horoscope; I just want one spot in the sky for you and me, side by side.

items.sourceNote: umbrella / sharing-shelter-in-the-rain theme, rewritten as a rainy-day dialogue

zh-tw.content:
「啊，突然下雨了，你有帶傘嗎？」
「沒有欸。」
「那剛好，我這把傘有點大，一個人撐很浪費，要不要一起？」
zh-tw.editorNote: 下雨天神級開場，自然又不油。重點是真的有把傘、而且真心想分一半，不要只是當台詞。共撐一把傘的距離本身就很加分，後面接『我送你到捷運站』收尾最順
variations: 雨下這麼大，我這把傘空著一半，借你站一下不用客氣
下雨了，與其各淋各的，不如我們共用這把，剛好我也想多跟你走一段

en.content:
"Oh, it just started raining — did you bring an umbrella?"
"Nope."
"Perfect, then. Mine's a little big for one person, kind of a waste. Want to share?"
en.editorNote: An elite rainy-day opener — natural, not slimy. The trick is to actually have the umbrella and genuinely mean the offer, not treat it as a script. Sharing one umbrella creates instant closeness; cap it with 'I'll walk you to the station.'
variations: It's really coming down — half my umbrella's empty anyway, hop under, no need to be shy.
Rather than both of us getting soaked, let's share this one — I wouldn't mind walking a bit longer with you.

items.sourceNote: Q&A-style 'what time is it / starting point of our happiness' line, reworded

zh-tw.content:
「現在幾點啦？」
「六點多吧。」
「不對欸，這是我們幸福的起點。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 一問一答型的萬用款，聊天冷掉或想偷偷撩一下都好用。重點是答得一臉認真，對方才會被反差煞到。曖昧期傳訊息收尾很順
variations: 你問我幾點？是我開始喜歡你的那一刻啦
幾點不重要，重要的是現在這刻有你

en.content:
"Hey, what time is it?"
"Like six-something."
"Nope — it's the starting point of our happiness."
en.editorNote: A versatile Q&A line for reviving a dead chat or sneaking in a little flirt. The trick is to deliver the answer with a totally straight face so the twist lands. Works great as a late-night text closer in the talking stage.
variations: You asked the time? It's the exact moment I started falling for you.
The time doesn't matter — what matters is you're in this one.

items.sourceNote: 'you look like a relative — my mom's daughter-in-law' joke line, reworded

zh-tw.content:
「你長得好像我一個親戚喔。」
「誰啊？」
「我媽的兒媳婦。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 搞笑型告白款，講出來八成會被打但氣氛超好。適合已經有點熟的曖昧對象，太生硬的人反而會尷尬。記得笑著講才不會油
variations: 你跟我一個未來的家人長超像欸——就是以後跟我同姓的那個
我媽看到你應該會很喜歡，她一直想要個這麼可愛的媳婦

en.content:
"You look exactly like one of my relatives."
"Which one?"
"My mom's future daughter-in-law."
en.editorNote: A goofy confession line — you'll probably get smacked, but the mood will be great. Best for someone you're already a little familiar with; it can land awkward on a total stranger. Say it with a grin so it doesn't come off slimy.
variations: You're a dead ringer for a future member of my family — the one who'll share my last name someday.
My mom would adore you; she's always wanted a daughter-in-law this cute.

items.sourceNote: 'you're acting weird today — cutely weird' Q&A line, reworded

zh-tw.content:
「你今天怪怪的欸。」
「哪裡怪？」
「怪可愛的。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 短小精悍的諧音收尾，傳訊息或當面講都行，反應快的話殺傷力很高。曖昧期想製造心跳很適合，太常用會破梗，留著關鍵時刻放
variations: 你最近真的不太對勁——可愛到有點犯規
我覺得你怪怪的，怪到我一直想看你

en.content:
"You're acting kind of weird today."
"Weird how?"
"Weirdly cute."
en.editorNote: A short, punchy wordplay closer that works in text or face-to-face — devastating if your timing's quick. Perfect for sparking butterflies in the talking stage; don't overuse it or the punchline wears off, so save it for the right moment.
variations: Something's been off about you lately — cute to the point of being illegal.
You seem weird to me — weird enough that I can't stop looking at you.

items.sourceNote: 'appendix — know nothing about you but should take you out' funny line, reworded

zh-tw.content:
「你知道你跟盲腸有點像嗎？」
「蛤？為什麼？」
「因為我對你一無所知，可是好想把你約出來。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 冷笑話路線，重點是英文裡『take you out』一語雙關（割掉／約出去），中文版就用『約出來』湊趣。適合幽默感對得上的人，講錯對象會很尷尬
variations: 你像我的盲腸——還沒搞懂你，就已經想把你帶走了
我對你了解不多，但莫名其妙就是想約你

en.content:
"Are you my appendix?"
"Um, why?"
"Because I know nothing about you, but I really feel like I should take you out."
en.editorNote: A pun-based corny line — 'take you out' works as both 'remove' and 'go on a date.' Best for someone whose sense of humor matches yours; aim it at the wrong person and it falls flat. Deliver it deadpan for max effect.
variations: You're like my appendix — I barely understand you, but I already want to take you out.
I don't know much about you, but for some reason I just want to ask you out.

items.sourceNote: 'even without gravity I'd still fall for you' smooth romantic line, reworded

zh-tw.content: 就算地球哪天沒了地心引力，我還是會繼續為你淪陷。
zh-tw.editorNote: 走甜路線的單句款，沒有引力照樣『往下掉／淪陷』的雙關。適合已經確認心意、想加溫的時候傳，曖昧初期講可能太重，斟酌使用
variations: 別人靠地心引力站著，我是靠喜歡你撐著
沒有引力大家都會飄走，只有我會一直往你那裡掉

en.content: Even if the Earth lost its gravity tomorrow, I'd still keep falling for you.
en.editorNote: A sweet one-liner riding on the 'fall' pun — works with or without gravity. Best once feelings are mutual and you want to turn up the warmth; it can feel too heavy early in the talking stage, so use your judgment.
variations: Everyone else stays grounded by gravity — I stay standing because I like you.
Without gravity everyone would drift off; I'd just keep falling toward you.

zh-tw.content:
「我手搖飲都點正常甜，今天破例改無糖。」
「為什麼？」
「想留點額度，因為等等看到你就夠甜了。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 排隊買飲料、揪外送時超好接的一句，把『無糖』的反差當鋪陳，最後再轉甜。曖昧初期到穩定期都通用，講完可以順勢問對方要喝什麼
variations: 我今天故意點無糖，怕喝完再看到你會甜到蛀牙
店員問我幾分糖，我說隨便，反正我的甜都給你了

en.content:
"I always get my drinks regular sweet, but today I went sugar-free."
"Why?"
"Saving room — seeing you in a bit is gonna be plenty sweet."
en.editorNote: An easy line to drop while waiting in line for boba or ordering takeout. Use the 'sugar-free' contrast as setup, then flip it sweet. Works from early talking stage to dating — follow up by asking what they want to order.
variations: Went sugar-free on purpose today — figured seeing you would already be too sweet otherwise.
Barista asked how sweet I wanted it; I said whatever, I already gave all my sweetness to you.

zh-tw.content:
「你知道咖啡豆最厲害的本事是什麼嗎？」
「磨成咖啡？」
「是讓我整天都『豆』在想你。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 諧音梗款，『豆』諧音『都』，搞笑路線。咖啡廳、早餐店、上班遞咖啡時最自然，講完記得自己先笑一下化解尷尬
variations: 我不喝美式了，因為我已經對你『苦』盡甘來
咖啡可以提神，但讓我一整天清醒的是你

en.content:
"You know what coffee beans are best at?"
"Getting ground up?"
"Keeping me 'bean' thinking about you all day."
en.editorNote: A pun line ('bean' / 'been'), squarely in the goofy lane. Most natural at a cafe, breakfast spot, or while handing someone a coffee — crack a little smile yourself afterward to ease the cringe.
variations: I quit drinking espresso — you already perk me up just fine.
Coffee keeps me awake, but you're the reason I'm up thinking all night.

zh-tw.content:
「你知道我最喜歡吃哪種麵嗎？」
「拉麵？」
「是你的心『裡面』。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 經典『麵／裡面』諧音的對話款，可愛又好懂。吃飯、宵夜、聊美食時順手就能丟，對方通常會邊翻白眼邊笑，效果很穩
variations: 我最愛的不是義大利麵，是住進你心裡面
別人挑麵看湯頭，我挑的是能不能住進你裡面

en.content:
"Wanna know my favorite kind of dish?"
"Pasta?"
"A spot in your heart — table for one, please."
en.editorNote: A cute, easy-to-get food line in dialogue form. Toss it out over dinner, late-night snacks, or any food chat — they'll usually roll their eyes and laugh, which means it landed.
variations: My favorite dish isn't on any menu — it's a reservation in your heart.
People pick restaurants by the reviews; I'm just hoping for a seat in your heart.

zh-tw.content:
「我最近在練習當植物。」
「蛤？為什麼？」
「因為我想光合作用，只要有你這道光就夠了。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 搞笑開場再轉甜的對話款，『當植物』的荒謬感會先讓對方愣住。聊到耍廢、養植物、曬太陽時很好接，重點是前面要講得一本正經
variations: 我决定當向日葵了，反正我整天都朝著你轉
我不用充電，因為看你一眼就滿格了

en.content:
"I've been practicing being a plant lately."
"Huh? Why?"
"So I can photosynthesize — turns out you're the only light I need."
en.editorNote: A goofy setup that flips sweet; the absurd 'being a plant' bit makes them pause first. Easy to drop when talking about lazing around, houseplants, or soaking up sun — just deliver the opener with a totally straight face.
variations: I've decided to be a sunflower — I spend all day turning toward you anyway.
I don't need to charge my battery; one look at you and I'm at full power.

zh-tw.content:
「你家的Wi-Fi是不是壞了？」
「沒有啊，好好的。」
「奇怪，那為什麼我一看到你就覺得訊號超強？」
zh-tw.editorNote: 科技梗的對話款，適合在咖啡廳或一起用手機時丟出來。重點是要假裝認真問，等對方一臉疑惑再翻轉
variations: 你是不是無線網路？因為我跟你之間連線超穩
我手機常常斷線，只有靠近你的時候滿格

en.content:
"Is your Wi-Fi down or something?"
"No, it's fine. Why?"
"Weird, because every time I see you the signal feels insanely strong."
en.editorNote: A tech-flavored line in dialogue form, perfect for a cafe or while you're both on your phones. The trick is to ask it dead seriously, then flip it once they look confused.
variations: Are you Wi-Fi? Because the connection between us never drops.
My phone keeps losing signal — funny how it's at full bars whenever you're near.

zh-tw.content:
「你知道恐龍為什麼會絕種嗎？」
「不知道，為什麼？」
「因為那時候還沒有你，牠們活著也沒意思。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 冷知識開場的搞笑款，荒謬感很強。聊到電影、動物、博物館時很好接，講的時候表情越認真越好笑
variations: 恐龍那麼大隻都消失了，但我對你的喜歡一直都在
你笑起來的威力，大概可以讓滅絕的恐龍都復活

en.content:
"Do you know why the dinosaurs went extinct?"
"No idea, why?"
"Because you weren't around yet, so there was no point sticking around."
en.editorNote: A fun-fact opener that flips goofy — high absurdity factor. Easy to drop when talking about movies, animals, or museums; the straighter your face, the harder it lands.
variations: Even something as huge as a dinosaur disappeared, but how I feel about you never will.
Your smile is powerful enough to bring the extinct dinosaurs roaring back.

zh-tw.content:
「我點的拿鐵好像在吃醋。」
「咖啡怎麼吃醋？」
「因為它再香，也比不上你坐在我對面這麼甜。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 咖啡約會專用，現場有飲料就能即興演出。看著手中的杯子說最自然，適合第一次約會破冰
variations: 想一起去喝咖啡嗎？因為我對你的好感，多到一杯裝不下
我的咖啡都涼了，因為光看你就忘了喝

en.content:
"I think my latte is getting jealous."
"How can coffee be jealous?"
"Because no matter how sweet it is, it can't compete with you sitting across from me."
en.editorNote: Made for coffee dates — improvise it whenever there's a drink in hand. Saying it while glancing at your cup feels most natural; great for breaking the ice on a first date.
variations: Want to grab coffee? Because I like you more than one cup could ever hold.
My coffee went cold — turns out I forgot to drink it while looking at you.

zh-tw.content:
「我最近都改吃素了。」
「為什麼突然吃素？」
「因為菜單上沒有你，那我只好天天想你。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 經典『你是我的菜』的延伸對話版，多繞一個彎反而更有梗。吃飯、點餐、聊減肥時都能接，講完記得補一個無辜的表情
variations: 別人挑菜看新不新鮮，我只挑你這一道
我不是不吃肉，是想把胃口都留給你

en.content:
"I've gone vegetarian lately."
"Why the sudden switch?"
"Because you're not on any menu, so I just have to crave you instead."
en.editorNote: A roundabout spin on the classic 'you're my type of dish' line — the extra detour makes it land better. Works over meals, ordering, or diet talk; follow up with your most innocent face.
variations: Other people pick produce by freshness; I only ever pick you.
It's not that I gave up meat — I'm just saving my whole appetite for you.

items.sourceNote: Adapted from the classic 'autocomplete / Siri' pun line

zh-tw.content:
「你是不是手機的自動選字？」
「為什麼這樣問？」
「因為我才打一個字，你就把我整句話補完了。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 科技諧音款，適合聊到手機、打字、傳訊息卡頓時順勢丟出。Z世代很有共鳴，講完記得一臉認真，效果更好
variations: 你是不是我的輸入法？因為沒有你，我連一句話都講不完整
你是不是預測文字？因為你總是猜中我下一步想靠近你

en.content:
"Are you my phone's autocomplete?"
"Why do you ask?"
"Because I only type one letter and you finish my whole sentence."
en.editorNote: A tech-flavored pun line — slip it in when you're talking about phones, typing, or a laggy keyboard. It lands well with a younger crowd; keep a straight face for max effect.
variations: Are you my keyboard? Because without you I can't finish a single sentence.
Are you predictive text? Because you always guess my next move toward you.

items.sourceNote: Adapted from the 'time / remember the minute I fell for you' line

zh-tw.content:
「請問現在幾點？」
「快三點了，怎麼了？」
「沒事，只是想記住我喜歡上你的那一分鐘。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 走浪漫路線的對話款，借問時間自然開場，最後一句輕輕轉甜。曖昧初期傳訊息或面對面都能用，語氣放輕別太用力
variations: 你知道現在幾點嗎？是我這輩子最想記住的一刻
幫我看一下時間，我想把遇見你的這一秒存進手機

en.content:
"Excuse me, do you have the time?"
"Almost three, why?"
"Oh, nothing — I just want to remember the exact minute I fell for you."
en.editorNote: A romantic dialogue line that uses asking for the time as a natural opener, then softens into the turn. Works over text or in person during the early flirty stage; keep your tone light.
variations: Do you know what time it is? Because this is the moment I most want to remember.
Check the time for me — I want to save the second I met you in my phone.

items.sourceNote: Adapted from the 'Disneyland / happiest place' line

zh-tw.content:
「聽說迪士尼是世界上最快樂的地方。」
「對啊，超想去的。」
「那他們一定沒站在你旁邊過。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 聊到旅遊、樂園、放假計畫時超好接，先順著對方的話，再用最後一句反轉送甜。適合已經聊得起來、想加一點溫度的階段
variations: 別人排隊進樂園找快樂，我只要看到你就有了
全世界最開心的地方？對我來說就是你笑出來的那一刻

en.content:
"They say Disneyland is the happiest place on Earth."
"Yeah, I've been dying to go."
"Then they've clearly never stood next to you."
en.editorNote: Easy to drop in when the talk turns to travel, theme parks, or vacation plans — agree first, then flip it sweet on the last line. Best once the conversation's already flowing and you want to add warmth.
variations: People line up at theme parks to find happiness; I just have to look at you.
The happiest place on Earth? For me it's the moment you start to laugh.

items.sourceNote: Adapted from coffee-themed pickup lines (latte / I like you a lot)

zh-tw.content:
「你是拿鐵嗎？」
「為什麼這樣問？」
「因為我每天早上第一個想到的就是你。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 約在咖啡廳或聊到喝什麼飲料時最自然，先問一句再接甜點收尾。適合早上傳訊息給對方當開場
variations: 你一定是手沖咖啡，因為你值得我慢慢花時間
別人靠咖啡因醒過來，我只要想到你就整個人精神了

en.content:
"Are you a latte?"
"Why do you ask?"
"Because you're the first thing I think about every morning."
en.editorNote: Lands best at a cafe or when the chat turns to drinks — ask first, then close on the sweet beat. Great as a morning opener over text.
variations: You must be a pour-over, because you're worth taking my time over.
Other people need caffeine to wake up; I just have to think about you.

items.sourceNote: Adapted from cheese / 'cheese to my macaroni' food line

zh-tw.content: 如果我是起司，你就是我的通心粉，少了你整碗都不對味。
zh-tw.editorNote: 一起吃飯或聊到美食時很好用，土到剛剛好又不會太肉麻，傳訊息配個食物照片效果更好
variations: 你是我的醬油，沒有你我整個人都淡而無味
我願意把最後一塊雞排分你，這你應該懂這代表什麼

en.content: If I'm the cheese, you're my macaroni — without you the whole bowl just isn't right.
en.editorNote: Perfect over a meal or when the talk turns to food; cheesy enough to land without getting mushy. Pairs well with a food photo over text.
variations: You're the soy sauce to my rice — without you I'm completely bland.
I'd give you my last slice of fried chicken, and you know what that means.

items.sourceNote: Adapted from space / stardust 'light up my universe' line

zh-tw.content:
「你該不會是星塵做的吧？」
「怎麼說？」
「因為你一出現，我整個宇宙都亮了。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 聊到星空、追劇看科幻片或晚上一起看星星時最對味，浪漫但不老套。適合想加重一點分量的告白場合
variations: 你大概是顆超新星，因為你一笑就把我整個人炸開了
別人抬頭找北極星，我只要看你的眼睛就不會迷路

en.content:
"Are you made of stardust?"
"What makes you say that?"
"Because the second you show up, my whole universe lights up."
en.editorNote: Best when the talk turns to stargazing or a sci-fi night in — romantic without being a cliche. Good for when you want to dial the confession up a notch.
variations: You must be a supernova, because one smile from you blows me away.
Other people look up for the North Star; I just need your eyes to never get lost.

items.sourceNote: Adapted from chemistry 'copper + tellurium = CuTe' line

zh-tw.content:
「你身上是不是含有銅跟碲？」
「蛤？為什麼？」
「因為你看起來超 Cu-Te（cute）的。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 理科生或喜歡冷知識梗的人會被戳中笑點，需要對方聽得懂元素符號才好笑，建議先確認對象再出招
variations: 你一定有 11 顆質子，因為你 sodium（so dang）好看
我們之間是不是有化學反應？因為我整個被你吸過去了

en.content:
"Are you made of copper and tellurium?"
"Huh? Why?"
"Because you're looking seriously Cu-Te."

variations: You blurred my vision, so by the rules I have to log your details.

Some people you fall for slowly. You're the kind I decided on at first glance.

items.sourceNote: 改寫自 dropped my coffee 笑話，重寫成對話版並加入咖啡日常情境

zh-tw.content:
「不好意思，你欠我一杯咖啡。」
「我哪有？」
「有啊，剛剛看到你的瞬間，我手上那杯就掉了。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 咖啡廳或便利商店巧遇的經典套路，講完可以順勢約對方再喝一杯，把搭訕變成邀約
variations: 你害我手抖打翻咖啡，這筆帳我看只能用一場約會來還
我那杯拿鐵是為你犧牲的，要不要陪我再買一杯

en.content:
"Excuse me, you owe me a coffee."
"How do I owe you a coffee?"
"Because the moment I saw you, I dropped mine."
en.editorNote: A classic for a chance encounter at a cafe or convenience store. Follow up by inviting them to grab another — it turns the line into an actual ask.
variations: You made me spill my coffee, so I think you owe me a date to make it right.
That latte gave its life for you. Care to help me replace it?

items.sourceNote: 改寫自 'warm cup of tea, comforting and dangerous' rizz line，翻成中文並改成飲料對比

zh-tw.content: 你給人的感覺，就像一杯剛泡好的熱奶茶，又溫暖、又危險，喝一口就回不去了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合形容那種讓人安心又心動的對象，傳訊息時很好用，最後一句留白讓對方自己腦補
variations: 別人是清水，你是那種喝過一次就戒不掉的飲料
你像微溫的奶茶，明明知道會上癮，我還是一口接一口

en.content: You feel like a fresh cup of milk tea — warm, a little dangerous, and impossible to put down after the first sip.
en.editorNote: Perfect for describing someone who feels both comforting and thrilling. Works great over text — the open-ended last line lets them fill in the rest.
variations: Most people are plain water. You're the drink I can't quit after one taste.
You're like warm milk tea — I know it's addictive, and I keep going back for more anyway.

items.sourceNote: 改寫自 fine-apple 諧音哏，加上自嘲收尾

zh-tw.content:
「如果你是一種水果，你一定是芒果。」
「為什麼？」
「因為我一看到你就忙得心慌（芒果）。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 諧音哏入門款，重點是講完要笑著看對方，土歸土但很討喜
variations: 你要是水果，肯定是榴槤，因為一聞到就讓我留戀（榴槤）
如果你是水果，你就是釋迦，因為看到你我整顆心都釋（釋迦）出去了

en.content:
"If you were a fruit, you'd be a melon."
"Why's that?"
"Because you're one in a melon."
en.editorNote: A quick two-line fruit pun for a chat opener — works best when you send it with zero context.
variations: If you were a fruit, you'd be a cutie-cumber.
You must be a grape, because you're one in a bunch.

items.sourceNote: 改寫自 favorite coffee drink first-date 哏，改成手搖飲在地版

zh-tw.content:
「你平常喝飲料都點什麼？」
「半糖少冰的奶茶吧。」
「我先記起來，這樣第一次約會我就知道要幫你買什麼了。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 問飲料順便暗示要約會，超級自然的進攻法，傳訊息時特別好用，對方很難拒絕
variations: 你咖啡都喝哪種？我先存著，下次見面直接幫你帶
記一下你的飲料口味，這算我們第一次約會的前置作業

en.content:
"What do you usually order when you get drinks?"
"Half-sugar milk tea, less ice."
"Noted. Now I'll know exactly what to grab you on our first date."
en.editorNote: Asks about their order while quietly locking in a date. Works especially well over text — hard to turn down.
variations: What's your go-to coffee? I'm saving it for next time so I can bring you one.
Logging your drink order — call it prep work for date number one.

items.sourceNote: 改寫自 did the sun come out / picture us together 哏，合併為天氣破冰版

zh-tw.content:
「今天天氣是不是放晴了？」
「沒有啊，外面還在下雨。」
「奇怪，那一定是你剛剛對我笑了一下。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 下雨天破冰神器，把對方的笑容當成太陽，甜度高但不油膩，適合面對面用
variations: 外面明明在下雨，我這邊怎麼突然變晴天，原來是你抬頭看了我一眼
我以為今天會是陰天，結果你一笑，整天都亮起來了

en.content:
"Did it just clear up outside?"
"No, it's still raining."
"Strange — then it must've been you smiling at me."
en.editorNote: A rainy-day icebreaker that turns their smile into sunshine. Sweet without being greasy — best delivered in person.
variations: It's pouring out there, so why did my whole sky just clear up? Oh — you looked at me.
I figured today would be gray, but one smile from you and the whole day lit up.

items.sourceNote: 改寫自 'I like you a latte' 咖啡哏，改成台灣手搖飲店場景

zh-tw.content:
「你是不是手搖飲店的招牌？」
「為什麼這樣問？」
「因為我每天都想點你，而且絕對是全糖。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 排隊買飲料時的破冰款，把對方比成最想喝的那一杯，輕鬆不油膩
variations: 你大概是大杯少冰，因為看到你我整個人就消暑了
別人都選微糖，但你這杯我只想要全糖正常冰

en.content:
"Are you the bestseller at the boba shop?"
"Why do you ask?"
"Because I'd order you every single day — and always extra sweet."
en.editorNote: An icebreaker for the drink-line wait. Casts them as your go-to order. Light and not greasy.
variations: You must be a large with light ice, because one look at you and I instantly cooled off.
Everyone else picks half-sugar, but you're the one cup I want at full sweetness.

items.sourceNote: 改寫自 'you melt my heart like chocolate' 巧克力哏，改成台灣常見的便利商店熱可可場景

zh-tw.content:
「你知道你比超商的熱可可還厲害嗎？」
「哪有？」
「熱可可只能暖手，你連我整顆心都融化了。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 冬天或冷氣房裡用最對味，溫度反差讓土味多了一點真誠
variations: 別人喝熱可可暖身，我看到你就從心裡暖起來
你是不是加了棉花糖，不然怎麼又甜又讓人捨不得喝完

en.content:
"You know you're better than the hot cocoa at the corner store?"
"How so?"
"Cocoa only warms my hands — you melt my whole heart."
en.editorNote: Best in winter or a too-cold air-conditioned room. The temperature contrast adds a little sincerity to the cheese.
variations: Other people drink cocoa to warm up; one look at you and I'm warm from the inside.
Did someone add marshmallows to you? Because you're so sweet I never want the moment to end.

items.sourceNote: 改寫自 'are we in a lab, the chemistry feels real' 化學哏，改成圖書館場景的安靜版

zh-tw.content:
「欸，這裡是圖書館對吧？」
「對啊，要小聲一點。」
「奇怪，那我們之間的化學反應怎麼這麼大聲。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 安靜場合的低聲撩，反差感很加分，適合一起讀書或排隊時用
variations: 我們明明在念書，怎麼我滿腦子都是你這一題
圖書館要保持安靜，可是我的心跳實在太吵了

en.content:
"Hey, this is the library, right?"
"Yeah, keep it down."
"Weird — then why is the chemistry between us this loud?"
en.editorNote: A whispered line for a quiet setting; the contrast does the work. Great while studying together or waiting in line.
variations: We're supposed to be studying, but the only thing on my mind is you.
The library says stay quiet, but my heartbeat clearly didn't get the memo.

items.sourceNote: 改寫自雨天系列 'my favorite forecast: 100% chance of you and me'，改成台灣氣象主播口吻

zh-tw.content:
「你有看今天的天氣預報嗎？」
「沒有欸，怎麼了？」
「降雨機率我不知道，但遇到你的機率剛剛好是百分之百。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 下雨天或一起躲雨時最好用，把尷尬的等雨變成撩人的機會
variations: 氣象說今天有雨，可是我這邊只預報到一整天想你的機率
外面在下雨，但我的世界因為你放晴了

en.content:
"Did you catch today's forecast?"
"Not really, why?"
"No idea about the rain — but the chance of running into you turned out to be a solid one hundred percent."
en.editorNote: Perfect while sheltering from the rain together; turns an awkward wait into a smooth opening.
variations: They forecast rain today, but over here it's a hundred percent chance of thinking about you.
It's pouring outside, yet somehow my whole world cleared up the moment you smiled.

items.sourceNote: 改寫自健身房系列 'do you believe in love at first rep'，改成台灣健身房搭訕情境

zh-tw.content:
「不好意思，可以問你一下嗎？」
「嗯？」
「你相信一組深蹲就愛上，還是我要再多做兩組給你看？」
zh-tw.editorNote: 健身房搭訕神句，自嘲又不油，動作停頓時丟出來最自然
variations: 你是不是我今天的訓練菜單？因為看到你我整個人都熱起來了
我不太會算重量，但你在我心裡的份量我倒是很清楚

en.content:
"Sorry, can I ask you something?"
"Sure, what's up?"
"Do you believe in love at first rep, or should I knock out a couple more sets to convince you?"
en.editorNote: A gym opener that's self-deprecating rather than sleazy; drop it during a rest between sets.
variations: Are you today's workout? Because one look at you and I'm already warmed up.
I'm bad at counting the weight on the bar, but I know exactly how much you mean to me.

items.sourceNote: 改寫自 'you must be a stopwatch, time stops when you show up' 碼表哏

zh-tw.content:
「你是不是計時器？」
「什麼？」
「因為你一出現，我的世界時間就停了。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 運動場或跑步機旁都能用，把計時裝置的哏轉成甜點
variations: 你是不是碼表？我一看到你，秒針好像就忘記要動了
跑步機上我盯著時間，結果時間全被你偷走了

en.content:
"Are you a stopwatch?"
"What?"
"Because the moment you show up, time in my whole world just stops."
en.editorNote: Works by the track or next to a treadmill; flips a timer gadget into something sweet.
variations: Are you a stopwatch? Because the second I saw you, the ticking just forgot to keep going.
I was watching the clock on the treadmill, and somehow you ran off with all my time.

items.sourceNote: 改寫自天氣系列 'you're the silver lining in every rainy day' 烏雲鑲金邊哏

zh-tw.content:
「你知道烏雲最厲害的地方是什麼嗎？」
「不知道欸。」
「就算再黑，邊邊都會鑲一圈光——而你就是我每個壞天氣裡的那圈光。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 情緒溫柔的文青款，適合陪對方度過低潮或雨天傳訊時用
variations: 再爛的天氣都會過去，但我想留下來當你的那道彩虹
你就是那種，會讓陰天也捨不得下雨的人

en.content:
"You know the best thing about a storm cloud?"
"No idea."
"No matter how dark it gets, there's always light around the edges — and you're that light on every gray day of mine."
en.editorNote: A gentler, poetic line; good for comforting someone through a rough patch or a rainy-day text.
variations: Every bad forecast passes eventually, but I'd like to stick around and be your rainbow.
You're the kind of person who makes even a cloudy sky reluctant to rain.

items.sourceNote: 音樂系列 'my heart was on shuffle until it found you' 隨機播放哏改寫

zh-tw.content:
「我的心以前都是隨機播放模式。」
「所以呢？」
「所以每首歌都跳來跳去。直到遇到你，才終於單曲循環。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合對方愛聽音樂或一起分享耳機時用，文青感剛好不會太重
variations: 你是不是我歌單裡最想跳過的那首？才怪，你是我唯一想重播一整天的
我的心本來是無限播放清單，遇到你之後只想聽你這一首

en.content:
"My heart used to be stuck on shuffle."
"And?"
"And every song kept skipping around. Then I met you, and now it's just you on repeat."
en.editorNote: Good when they're into music or you're sharing earbuds; gentle and a little poetic without going overboard.
variations: Are you the one track I'd skip on my playlist? Nope — you're the only one I'd replay all day.
My heart was an endless playlist, but since I met you I only want to hear your song.

items.sourceNote: WiFi/連線哏 'I'm feeling a strong connection' 改寫成台灣手機沒訊號的日常

zh-tw.content:
「奇怪，我手機一格訊號都沒有。」
「這裡收訊本來就爛。」
「可是我跟你之間，明明連線超穩的欸。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 電梯裡、地下室、收訊差的地方臨場發揮最自然，理工宅也很好上手
variations: 你是不是我的WiFi？因為只要你不在，我整個人就斷線
別人要密碼才能連，我看到你就自動配對成功了

en.content:
"Weird, my phone's got zero bars."
"Yeah, the signal's terrible here."
"Strange, though — the connection between you and me is rock solid."
en.editorNote: Plays perfectly in an elevator, a basement, or anywhere with bad reception; easy for the tech-nerd type too.
variations: Are you my WiFi? Because the second you're gone, I completely lose connection.
Everyone else needs a password to connect — with you I paired up automatically.

items.sourceNote: 甜點系列 'you're sweet as pie / the cream in my coffee' 改寫成台灣手搖飲場景

zh-tw.content:
「我剛剛跟店員說飲料要無糖。」
「你不是最愛喝甜的嗎？」
「因為有你在旁邊，這杯本來就夠甜了。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 手搖飲、飲料店場景超好用，台味十足，講完記得害羞地笑一下
variations: 微糖就好，反正甜的部分你已經負責了
我點無糖不是怕胖，是因為你一坐過來，我這桌甜度直接爆表

en.content:
"I just told them I want my drink with no sugar."
"But you always get it sweet."
"With you sitting next to me, this cup is already sweet enough."
en.editorNote: Made for a bubble-tea or drink-stand moment; very local flavor — follow it with a shy little grin.
variations: Just a little sugar's fine — you've already handled the sweet part.
I didn't order it unsweetened to cut calories; it's because the moment you sat down, this whole table maxed out on sweetness.

items.sourceNote: 咖啡系 'I like you a latte' 諧音梗改寫成台灣咖啡廳點餐場景

zh-tw.content:
「你要點什麼？」
「一杯拿鐵，還有你。」
「我又不在菜單上。」
「可是我對你的喜歡，早就爆單了。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 咖啡廳、早午餐店排隊點餐時最自然，講完可以順勢問要不要一起坐
variations: 我拿鐵少冰半糖，但對你這件事我完全不加控制
菜單上沒有你，害我看半天都不知道要點什麼

en.content:
"What can I get you?"
"One latte — and you."
"I'm not on the menu."
"Maybe not, but my crush on you sold out ages ago."
en.editorNote: Works best in a coffee shop or brunch line; follow it up by asking if they want to grab a seat together.
variations: I take my latte light ice, half sweet — but when it comes to you I keep no limits at all.
You're not on the menu, which is why I've been staring at it forever with no idea what to order.

items.sourceNote: 圖書館系 'checking you out' 借書梗改寫成台灣圖書館/書店場景

zh-tw.content:
「你在找哪一本？」
「其實我早就找到了。」
「在哪一區？」
「就在我旁邊，而且我很想把你借回家。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 圖書館、二手書店、誠品都好用，聲音記得放輕才不會被館員瞪
variations: 這本我看不懂沒關係，反正我只想一直翻你這一頁
別人的書要蓋章才能借，你不用，你直接住進我心裡就好

en.content:
"Which book are you looking for?"
"Honestly, I already found it."
"Which section?"
"Right next to me — and I really want to check you out."
en.editorNote: Great for a library, a used-book store, or a quiet bookshop; keep your voice down so the staff don't glare.
variations: It's fine that I don't understand this book — I only want to keep turning to your page.
Everyone else's book needs a stamp to borrow; you don't — you just move straight into my heart.

items.sourceNote: 天文系 'you control my tides / light up my sky' 改寫成台灣夜市看月亮場景

zh-tw.content:
「你看今天月亮好圓。」
「對啊，超亮的。」
「不過在我這邊，最亮的又不是月亮。」
「不然是什麼？」
「是正在抬頭看它的你。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 河堤散步、夜市回家路上、跨年倒數前都很加分，抬頭看月亮那句要慢慢講
variations: 月亮會有陰晴圓缺，可是我對你的心一直是滿的
大家都在拍月亮，只有我一直偷拍你

en.content:
"Look how full the moon is tonight."
"Yeah, it's so bright."
"Funny thing is, on my side the moon isn't the brightest thing here."
"Then what is?"
"You — the one looking up at it."
en.editorNote: Earns big points on a riverside walk, the way home from a night market, or right before a New Year countdown; deliver the moon line slowly.
variations: The moon waxes and wanes, but my heart for you stays full the whole time.
Everyone's photographing the moon — I'm the only one secretly photographing you.

items.sourceNote: 健身系 'suddenly motivated to commit' 改寫成台灣健身房場景

zh-tw.content:
「你今天練哪裡？」
「本來要練腿。」
「那怎麼站在這發呆？」
「因為我看到你之後，決定改練專情。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 健身房、運動場館搭訕專用，講完可以順便問要不要幫忙補位
variations: 我今天最大的重量，是抬頭看你那一下的心跳
教練說我核心不穩，可能是因為看到你就腳軟

en.content:
"What are you training today?"
"I was gonna do legs."
"So why are you just standing here spacing out?"
"Because after seeing you, I decided to train commitment instead."
en.editorNote: Made for the gym or a sports center; follow it up by offering to spot them.
variations: My heaviest lift today was my heartbeat the moment I looked up at you.
Coach says my core is unstable — probably because my knees go weak the second I see you.

items.sourceNote: 起司主題 'gouda / melting' 梗，改寫成台灣夜市牽絲起司場景

zh-tw.content:
「你知道我最喜歡什麼起司嗎？」
「不知道，什麼？」
「你這種的，因為看到你，我整個人都在牽絲了。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 逛夜市、吃牽絲起司馬鈴薯或起司熱狗時用，講完可以分對方一口
variations: 你一定是高融點起司，因為別人融化了還撐得住，我看到你直接融化
我對起司過敏，但為了你我願意天天牽絲

en.content:
"You know my favorite kind of cheese?"
"No, what?"
"Your kind — because one look at you and I'm already a stretchy, melty mess."
en.editorNote: Perfect over street-food cheese fries or a cheese-pull hot dog; offer them a bite after.
variations: You must be high-melt cheese, because everyone else holds their shape and I fall apart the second I see you.
I'm lactose intolerant, but for you I'd get the cheese pull every single day.

items.sourceNote: 咖啡 'woke up my whole personality' 梗，改寫成台灣早餐店/咖啡廳場景

zh-tw.content:
「你是不是加了兩份濃縮？」
「沒有啊，怎麼了？」
「因為我一看到你，整個人瞬間清醒，心跳還飆得比咖啡因還快。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 早餐店、咖啡廳排隊時搭訕用，可以順口問要不要幫對方一起點
variations: 別人喝咖啡提神，我看你一眼就整天不用睡了
你是我的手沖，慢慢來但一口就上頭

en.content:
"Did you get a double shot of espresso?"
"No, why?"
"Because the second I saw you I snapped wide awake, and my heart's racing harder than any caffeine could do."
en.editorNote: Use it in line at a cafe or breakfast spot; offer to add their order to yours.
variations: Other people need coffee to wake up — one look at you and I'm set for the whole day.
You're my pour-over: worth the wait, and one sip completely goes to my head.

items.sourceNote: 披薩 'cheesy but still a great idea' 梗，改寫成台灣宵夜約會場景

zh-tw.content:
「我這句話應該很土吧？」
「還好，你想說什麼？」
「你是不是披薩？就算再土，跟你在一起永遠都是好主意。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 約宵夜、一起叫外送披薩時用，講完可以問要不要各出一半錢再一起吃
variations: 你是我的最後一片披薩，明知道不該搶，但我還是想留給自己
別人怕肥不敢吃，我看到你倒是完全不想節制

en.content:
"This line's probably super corny, huh?"
